metaDescription: Detect a blanket Disallow: / or noindex that was pushed from staging to production, or a staging site left open. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Checks whether the robots.txt you paste blocks ordinary pages, and whether the page headers or HTML carry noindex, for production or staging.
why:
One of the classic launch mistakes is shipping the staging robots.txt (Disallow: /) or a noindex tag to production. Traffic falls over days and nobody sees why. The reverse also happens: a staging site left open gets indexed.

Paste the live robots.txt, optionally the headers and page head, and say which environment it is. The tool checks the root and a deep page for * and the big crawlers and tells you what to review.
howTo: Paste the robots.txt your site serves.
Optionally paste response headers and the page head.

faq.q: Does robots.txt hide a staging site?
faq.a: It asks crawlers to stay out, but it is not security. Use a password.
A noindex tag has the same effect on search as a block and is often forgotten.

faq.q: Will it check my live site?
faq.a: No, it only reads what you paste. Fetching a site needs a network request.

faq.q: How can I avoid the mistake?
faq.a: Add a robots.txt and noindex check to your release checklist.
